History, and the duplicate-invoice lookup behind the FR8 warning.

`invoice_no` stays an exact-match lookup — it answers "was this invoice processed
before", which is a different question from the `q` search box.

patch.description: Rename a batch. Allowed in any status — a name is metadata, not output.

get.description:
A single generated file.

`name` must be a key of the job's artifact manifest. The job directory also holds
the uploaded PDFs, the report, and the raw AI request/response logs; serving from
the manifest rather than the directory is what keeps those unreachable.

The batch as a zip, optionally narrowed to chosen files.

Choosing files is a packaging decision, not a partial result: every artifact is
still generated and kept. Selecting everything (or nothing) serves the archive the
run already built, so the common path stays byte-identical to what it produced.

Parts whose HSN is blank or still provisional, with any remembered code.

A remembered code is offered as a *suggestion* with its own provenance shown — it is
never pre-applied as though somebody had typed it.

post.description:
Re-run a completed batch from its stored extractions, optionally filling HSNs.

Costs no tokens: every document is replayed from the extraction cache. The source
job is superseded, never modified — its CSVs are already in Zoho.

Settle a blocked batch's reader disagreements and run it again.

Only disagreements about a line's manufacturer or description can be settled, and
every blocking finding must be: anything else (a quantity, a price, a part number,
a tariff code) stays a hard block. The answers are checked against the blocked
job's own report, recorded with the caller's name, and applied to a new job that
replays the stored extractions, so it costs no tokens. The blocked job is kept.

Attach a late-arriving Bill of Entry to a batch that was processed without one.

The invoices are replayed from the source batch's stored PDFs, so only the BOE is
sent to the model. The result supersedes the source job and carries an Items Update
CSV for exactly the parts whose HSN the BOE changed (FR12).

put.description: Replace the batch's user tags. Pipeline-applied tags are left alone.

get.description:
Everything needed to answer "why did this batch produce that".

Available for **every** status, deliberately — unlike the file endpoints, which
require `done`. A failed run is exactly the one you most need to read back, and
refusing to trace it would leave the raw model response reachable only by logging
in to the host.

One raw AI request or response, as this run recorded it.

`name` is matched against the job's log index before any path is built from it, so
the uploaded PDFs and the generated CSVs sitting in the same directory stay
unreachable through this route.

Replace the item-master snapshot with one Zoho org's item export.

`org_id` names the org the export came from; omitted, it is the default org (the
oldest active one), which is what every upload before the org model meant.

post.description:
Group purchase orders into RE-numbered sales invoices.

Several groups in one call, because that is how the work actually arrives — a
session's worth is two or three invoices, each covering a few consignments.

All or nothing: if any group is refused, none is written. A partly applied grouping
leaves purchase orders invoiced that nobody meant to invoice, and D02 would then
refuse to put them right.
